pr_title: Fix MQTT rgb light brightness scaling
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

When the brightness of MQTT rgb light is scaled and, the current brightness calculated from the rgb status, this should be taken into account when setting a new brightness.

Example: When the brightness is first set to 128 (50%) on a rgb of (255,0,0) the result is (128,0,0). If then the brightness is set to 191 (75 %) we should know that the current RGB values are related to the current brightness.

issue_context.title: Cannot increase brightness on MQTT RGB light
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a manually configured MQTT RGB light as follows:
```
mqtt:
  light:
      - name: "Pool light"
        unique_id: "pool_light"
        state_topic: "pool/light"
        command_topic: "pool/cmd/light"
        rgb_state_topic: "pool/light/rgb"
        rgb_command_topic: "pool/cmd/light/rgb"
        qos: 0
        payload_on: "ON"
        payload_off: "OFF"
        optimistic: false
        retain: true
```
The light has no separate brightness control, the brightness is changed by altering the RGB values directly. Once the light receives a command, it merely echoes the MQTT message back on the state topics.

If I set it to some arbitrary color, then lower the brightness, I can no longer increase the brightness. If I try, HA lowers the brightness even more (the slider briefly goes up and then down further - I assume once it receives the state topic, which is exactly what it sent in the command topic). I checked the messages on MQTT Explorer and there is no funny business happening - when I increase the brightness slider on HA, it simply sends a command message with a lower one; there is no message with higher RGB values before the one with lower values. 

I can work around the problem by commenting out the `rgb_state_topic` line on the YAML code, but that is not ideal since HA looses track of the light's color if it is changed externally. I suppose once HA receives the RGB values in the state topic it somehow calculates a wrong brightness from them...

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Home Assistant 2023.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

can't remember, probably before year-month versions, it's been a long time since I tried changing the brightness on HA

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

MQTT Light

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.mqtt/

### Diagnostics information

```
 "light": [
        {
          "name": "Pool light",
          "unique_id": "pool_light",
          "state_topic": "pool/light",
          "command_topic": "pool/cmd/light",
          "rgb_state_topic": "pool/light/rgb",
          "rgb_command_topic": "pool/cmd/light/rgb",
          "qos": 0,
          "payload_on": "ON",
          "payload_off": "OFF",
          "optimistic": false,
          "retain": true,
          "schema": "basic",
          "white_scale": 255,
          "brightness_scale": 255,
          "payload_available": "online",
          "enabled_by_default": true,
          "on_command_type": "last",
          "payload_not_available": "offline",
          "encoding": "utf-8",
          "availability_mode": "latest"
        }
      ],
      "broker": "core-mosquitto",
      "password": "**REDACTED**",
      "username": "**REDACTED**"
```

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
mqtt:
  light:
      - name: "Pool light"
        unique_id: "pool_light"
        state_topic: "pool/light"
        command_topic: "pool/cmd/light"
        rgb_state_topic: "pool/light/rgb"
        rgb_command_topic: "pool/cmd/light/rgb"
        qos: 0
        payload_on: "ON"
        payload_off: "OFF"
        optimistic: false
        retain: true
```

Can you indicate in steps what commands you give in the UI, what payloads you receive on which topics, and then explain what the actual and expected behavior?

1. User: turn light on on UI
2. HA: `pool/cmd/light ON`
3. Light: `pool/light ON`
4. UI: shows light on
5. User: set light color to blue on UI color wheel
6. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,255`
7. Light: `pool/light/rgb 0,0,255`
8. UI: displays 100% brightness blue light
9. User: change brightness to 50% on UI
10. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,128`
11. Light: `pool/light/rgb 0,0,128`
12. UI: displays 50% brightness (until now everything is expected behavior)
13. User: try to increase brightness to 75% on UI
14. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,95`  # expected: 0,0,191
15. Light: `pool/light/rgb 0,0,95`
16. UI: now displays 37% brightness
17. User: try to increase brightness to 50% on UI
18. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,47`  # expected: 0,0,128
19. Light: `pool/light/rgb 0,0,47`
20. UI: now displays 18% brightness
21. User: try to increase brightness to 100% on UI
22. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,47`  # expected: 0,0,255
23. Light: `pool/rgb 0,0,47`
24. UI: now displays 100% brightness (expected for rgb_state_topic received: remain on 18% brightness)
25. UI: User: try to change brightness to 50% on UI
26. HA: `pool/cmd/light/rgb 0,0,23`  # expected: 0,0,128
27. Light: `pool/light/rgb 0,0,23`
28. UI: now displays 9% brightness 
29. Continue and eventually brightness goes to 1% and RGB values to 0,0,1
Thnx for reporting, I was able to reproduce the bug. I now need to see where it goes wrong with the brightness calculation.

When the new brightness value is set, the current RGB value are related to the current brightness.
I opened a PR for a Fix, that I believe should fix your issue.

@tracestep while there's indeed a bug in MQTT light, an RGB light without a separate brightness control is a terrible idea and does not work well.

Lets say the user tries to set the light to this pink-ish color, with a very very low brightness:
rgb = (255, 127, 127), brightness = 1
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14281572/223366887-583ee9ae-8943-4ec4-a4d7-c0e5e7538121.png)


HA will send this message your light:
`pool/cmd/light/rgb "1,0,0"`
It means we only have a single bit of precision left instead of 8.

Your light confirms the state update:
`pool/light/rgb "1,0,0"`

The bug is that Home Assistant incorrectly interprets that message like this:
rgb = (1, 0, 0), brightness = 1

However, even if Home Assistant correctly interprets that message, the best it can do is this:
rgb = (255, 0, 0), brightness = 1

This means we've lost basically all color information, and if the user increases the brightness, the light will be red instead of pink:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14281572/223366976-6e7af23a-e4fb-428f-8069-0862002062b6.png)

Thanks, @jbouwh!

@emontnemery, not having separate brightness controls is exactly how RGB lights themselves work... all they have for the drivers is one PWM signal (usually with 8-bit precision) for each of the emitters. Brightness would always be calculated to/from these values, whether by HA or by the firmware in the light. 

All lights will lose color precision on very low brightness; then it's just a software design decision on how to deal with low brightness and how to restore "original" brightness, like calculating brightness based on how far all three values are from 255, or maintaining a register for the color at 100% brightness (the color chosen on the UI color wheel).

If I choose a pink color rgb=(255,127,137), HA can "decide" that 1% brightness is rgb=(2,1,1), not (1,0,0);  if, at first, HA has no other information on the color than (rgb = 1,0,0), it can very well decide that this is a pure red light at 0,5% brightness. The same holds true for the light's firmware if HA sends it rgb=(1,0,0) and X% brightness.

> not having separate brightness controls is exactly how RGB lights themselves work... all they have for the drivers is one PWM signal (usually with 8-bit precision) for each of the emitters. 

Yes, that's how the _hardware_ works a the lowest level, but since Home Assistant allows the user to adjust brightness independently of the color, you need to do either of:
a) keep track of both color and brightness in your MQTT light, and scale the color by the brightness when setting the PWM channels
b) configure the light to be optimistic, meaning it doesn't send any RGB state updates back
@jbouwh I almost think it's worth considering not allowing configuring a light with an `rgb_state_topic` but no `brightness_state_topic`?
@tracestep Out of curiosity, what software is controlling your light?

Well, it's an ESP32 Arduino project I developed a "long" time ago that controls pool heating, filling, pH, pumping, lighting and a bunch of other things via MQTT, and that by now I have forgotten enough about to be afraid to mess with. Besides, the hardware is hard to reach and has no OTA. So it seemed sensible to make the firmware as dumb as possible and implement all the intelligence in automations and through HA itself. Hence, no separate brightness, just RGB values that go straight to the PWM drivers. I normally leave it at full brightness and change only the color, but occasionally color updates through Google Assistant cause the calculated brightness to go down. 

I would be ok with not having brightness controls if I could choose the color, but I see no reason to not allow rgb topics without a brightness topic. It would be a great loss of functionality only for the sake of some side-effects. And there are probably RGB lights out there that work just like this whose firmware cannot be changed.

@tracestep I see. I think your best option is to remove the `rgb_state_topic: "pool/light/rgb"`, then the MQTT light will keep track of the color and brightness internally, meaning it's possible to dim the light without forgetting the color 🤷‍♂️

review_comments: We should not just check the brightness, we should also check the rgb_color attribute
